question: What is the primary definition of histology?

options.A: The study of tissues and their structures
options.B: The measurement of body fluid volumes
options.C: The microscopic examination of single isolated cells
options.D: The analysis of whole organ systems

explanation: Histology is specifically dedicated to examining the microscopic anatomy and arrangement of tissues. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: How do tissues and membranes relate structurally within the human body?

options.A: Membranes exist independently without cellular tissue components
options.B: Membranes dissolve into fluid before forming any tissue
options.C: Tissues combine together to form sheet-like membranes
options.D: Tissues are only found on the external skin surface

explanation: Body membranes are organized combinations of epithelial and connective tissues working together to cover and line structures. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which primary tissue type is primarily responsible for covering body surfaces and lining internal cavities?
explanation: Epithelial tissue forms the protective outer layers and lines internal passageways and cavities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: What distinguishes connective tissue from the other primary tissue categories?

options.A: It consists exclusively of tightly packed living cells with no matrix
options.B: It contains an abundant extracellular matrix surrounding cells
options.C: It lacks any blood supply entirely throughout the body
options.D: It generates electrical impulses for voluntary motor movement

explanation: Unlike tightly packed epithelia, connective tissues are defined by widely spaced cells embedded in a rich extracellular matrix of fibers and ground substance. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which type of body membrane lines freely movable joint cavities to secrete lubricating fluid?
explanation: Synovial membranes are purely connective tissue structures that line joint capsules and produce synovial fluid for smooth articulation. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is the primary physiological role of serous membranes in the thoracic and abdominopelvic cavities?

options.A: Absorbing dietary nutrients from the gastrointestinal tract
options.B: Generating voluntary contractions to pump blood through vessels
options.C: Reducing friction between constantly moving internal organs
options.D: Providing a tough, keratinized barrier against bacterial entry

explanation: Serous membranes secrete a watery fluid that lubricates the parietal and visceral layers, preventing friction damage as organs move. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h3)

question: What term describes the replacement of destroyed tissue with fibrous scar tissue?
explanation: Fibrosis is the repair process where fibroblasts lay down collagen fibers, creating scar tissue when full cellular regeneration is impossible. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: Why do cardiac muscle cells experience permanent functional deficits following a myocardial infarction?

options.A: They are protected by dense synovial fluid within the heart
options.B: They have extremely limited capacity for mitotic cell division
options.C: They are constantly replaced by rapidly dividing epithelial cells
options.D: They lack any blood supply to deliver oxygen and nutrients

explanation: Cardiac muscle cells are terminally differentiated and cannot divide to replace dead cells, resulting in fibrous scar replacement. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h4)

question: A patient with prolonged immobility develops a pressure ulcer over the sacrum. Which underlying tissue layers are primarily compromised in this clinical scenario?

options.A: Nervous tissue of the central brain parenchyma
options.B: Serous membranes of the abdominal peritoneal cavity
options.C: Synovial membranes and cartilage matrices exclusively

explanation: Pressure ulcers originate at the skin surface and subcutaneous layers due to sustained mechanical pressure and ischemia. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct goal of nursing care when managing a surgical wound healing by secondary intention?

options.A: Maintaining a clean, moist environment for granulation
options.B: Encouraging complete necrosis of the wound edges
options.C: Providing proper nutritional support for protein synthesis
options.D: Promoting adequate tissue perfusion and oxygenation

explanation: Nurses aim to prevent necrosis, infection, and further tissue damage, not encourage tissue death. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T8#GNS111_U1_T8_h5)
